name: Pallu
title: Son of Reuben
summary: Pallu was the second son of Reuben, Jacob's firstborn. He was one of the Israelites who went down to Egypt with Jacob's family. He is the ancestor of the Palluites, a clan within the tribe of Reuben, and his descendants played a role in Israel's history, including the rebellion of Dathan and Abiram.

keyEvents.title: Jacob's family moves to Egypt
keyEvents.description: Pallu was among Jacob's descendants who went down to Egypt with the whole family during the time when Joseph was vizier in Egypt.

keyEvents.title: Registered as a son of Reuben
keyEvents.description: Pallu is mentioned as the second son of Reuben in the genealogies, and his descendants became a recognized clan in Israel.

keyEvents.title: The clan of the Palluites
keyEvents.description: At the census in the wilderness, Pallu's descendants, the Palluites, were registered as a distinct clan within the tribe of Reuben.

keyEvents.title: Lineage to Eliab
keyEvents.description: Pallu's son Eliab became the father of Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram, who later became known in Israel's history.

keyEvents.title: Connection to Korah's rebellion
keyEvents.description: Pallu's grandchildren Dathan and Abiram, sons of Eliab, rebelled against Moses and Aaron in the wilderness along with Korah, and were swallowed by the earth as God's judgment.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in 1 Chronicles
keyEvents.description: Pallu is also recorded in the genealogies in 1 Chronicles as a son of Reuben, confirming his place in Israel's tribal history.
